messages.content:
You tailor resume bullets to a job posting without changing what is true. You get facts about one experience, each with an id, and the bullets now on the resume. Rewrite each bullet for the posting and cite the facts it rests on.

Rules. A verifier checks them, and a bullet that breaks one is thrown away and replaced by the original, so do not push against them:
1. No new numbers. Every number must come from a fact you cite; do not add, combine or compute.
2. No new technologies, products or proper nouns that the cited facts or the tech list do not name.
3. No absolute words (never, always, guaranteed, zero, every, all, exactly-once, 100%) unless a cited fact says so.
4. No causes or mechanisms the facts do not state: "by X", "through X", "so that X" only where a fact links X to that result.
5. Round only the unflattering way: show a number as written or rounded down, never up (3,781 may become 3.7K+, never 3.8K+).
6. Use the posting's words only where they describe this work accurately.
Also: respect the "must not claim" list, keep each bullet to one sentence, start it with a past-tense verb, and put every fact you used in sources.
Return exactly as many bullets as you are asked for, in the order given.

Posting: Site Reliability Engineer at Basalt Wharf Cloud
Responsibilities:
- Own the availability targets for our core services: define service level objectives, track error budgets and decide with product teams when to slow down.
- Run and improve the Kubernetes clusters that host our services, including upgrades, capacity planning and autoscaling.
- Manage infrastructure as code with Terraform, and review changes from other teams for safety.
- Build monitoring and alerting with Prometheus and Grafana that points at causes instead of symptoms.
- Lead incident response, write blameless postmortems and follow the action items through.
- Automate toil in Python or Go and push the on-call load down quarter by quarter.
Requirements:
- Three or more years running production services on a major cloud, preferably AWS.
- Hands-on experience with Kubernetes, Linux and networking fundamentals.
- A record of reducing alert noise or incident counts that you can describe with numbers.
- Clear written communication: runbooks, postmortems and design notes.
Keywords:
- Kubernetes
- Terraform
- Prometheus
- Grafana
- Python
- Go
- Linux
- Networking
- AWS
- PostgreSQL
- Service meshes
- Chaos testing
- Progressive delivery
- Backup and restore drills

Experience: Tidekv: an embedded key-value store in Go
Tech list: Go, Make, pprof, GitHub Actions
Facts you may cite:
[tidekv#1] Built an embedded key-value store in Go with a write-ahead log, an in-memory memtable and sorted tables on disk, and recovered the memtable from a log of 8,000 records in 120 ms.
[tidekv#2] Raised single-threaded write throughput from 7,200 to 18,000 writes/s by enlarging the write buffer from 4 MB to 64 MB, which cut flushes from 910 to 140.
[tidekv#3] Cut the compaction of a 6 GB data set from 91 s to 29.5 s, a 3.08x speed-up, by merging 4 tables at a time instead of 2.
[tidekv#4] Lost no acknowledged write across 200 seeded crash-injection runs, each checked against an in-memory model after recovery.
[tidekv#5] Added a read-only follower that tails the write-ahead log; 2,000 randomized reads returned the same values on the follower and the leader.
[tidekv#scope] ORIGIN: personal project, written to learn how storage engines recover from crashes. EVIDENCE: bench/results-2025-06.csv (one 8-core laptop with NVMe; one writer goroutine; median of 5 runs; the throughput gain is attributed to the larger write buffer by the flush counts, 910 down to 140); the recovery test replays a log of exactly 8,000 records; the 6 GB compaction input is synthetic; the crash test is test/crash_test.go (200 seeds, no acknowledged write lost, the model compared after every recovery); the follower test is test/follower_test.go (2,000 randomized reads).
Must not claim:
- production use or real users (it has only run on one laptop and in CI)
- multi-writer throughput (only one writer goroutine was benchmarked, and the gain came from the write buffer)
- durability guarantees beyond the 200 tested crashes (power-loss behaviour of the disk was not tested)
- read scaling or follower throughput (the follower's speed was never measured)
- any comparison with other storage engines (none was run)

Bullets to rewrite (return exactly 3; bullet k is the rewrite of k):
1. Built an embedded key-value store in Go with a write-ahead log, an in-memory memtable and sorted tables on disk, and recovered the memtable from a log of 8,000 records in 120 ms.
2. Added a read-only follower that tails the write-ahead log; 2,000 randomized reads returned the same values on the follower and the leader.
3. Raised single-threaded write throughput from 7,200 to 18,000 writes/s by enlarging the write buffer from 4 MB to 64 MB, which cut flushes from 910 to 140.

[tidekv#1]"}, {"sources": ["tidekv#5"], "text": "Ensured data consistency across leader and follower nodes through randomized reads, confirming identical values after tailing the write-ahead log. [tidekv#5]"}, {"sources": ["tidekv#2"], "text": "Improved single-threaded write throughput from 7,200 to 18,000 writes/s by increasing the write buffer to 64 MB, reducing flushes from 910 to 140. [tidekv#2]"}]}

The verifier rejected these bullets:
Bullet 1 was rejected. You wrote: 'Designed a storage engine with a write-ahead log, in-memory memtable, and sorted disk tables, achieving 120 ms recovery time for 8,000-record logs. [tidekv#1]'
  - escalation_causal: 'with a write-ahead log' - the cited sources do not link 'with a write-ahead log' to the result in one statement
  - fabricated_number: '1' - no count in the sources equals '1'; the sources have 8,000
Bullet 2 was rejected. You wrote: 'Ensured data consistency across leader and follower nodes through randomized reads, confirming identical values after tailing the write-ahead log. [tidekv#5]'
  - escalation_causal: 'through randomized reads' - the cited sources do not link 'through randomized reads' to the result in one statement
  - fabricated_number: '5' - no count in the sources equals '5'; the sources have 2,000
Bullet 3 was rejected. You wrote: 'Improved single-threaded write throughput from 7,200 to 18,000 writes/s by increasing the write buffer to 64 MB, reducing flushes from 910 to 140. [tidekv#2]'
  - fabricated_number: '2' - no count in the sources equals '2'; the sources have 140, 910

Rewrite only these 3 bullets, in the order listed, so that none of the problems remains. If a bullet cannot be improved within the rules, return the original bank wording of that bullet with the fact ids it comes from.

bullets.text: Built an embedded key-value store in Go with a write-ahead log, in-memory memtable, and sorted disk tables. Recovered the memtable from an 8,000-record log in 120 ms. [tidekv#1]
Conducted 2,000 randomized reads to verify data consistency between leader and follower nodes after tailing the write-ahead log. [tidekv#5]
Improved single-threaded write throughput from 7,200 to 18,000 writes/s by increasing the write buffer to 64 MB, reducing flushes from 910 to 140. [tidekv#2]
